newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fay Richwhite files High Court Action.
newsitem.headline: Fay Richwhite files High Court Action.

text.p: Fay Richwhite and Co Ltd said on Wednesday it had filed proceedings in the High Court at Auckland to review the conduct of the Commission of Inquiry into the "Winebox" affair.

Fay Richwhite principal David Richwhite told a news conference the company had decided to bring proceedings after what he said was the "recent revelation" that secret evidence had been heard by the Commissioner of the Inquiry, Sir Ronald Davison.
Richwhite said Davison had heard secret evidence in private two years ago and it had not been disclosed to the affected parties.

He said Fay Richwhite had found out about the existence of the interviews in an article in Metro magazine and applied to the Commissioner to obtain transcripts which were then provided on a confidential basis.
The statement of claim filed today sought to review the conduct of the Commission of Inquiry on the grounds of bias, predetermination, breach of natural justice and unfairness.
"Every New Zealander is entitled to expect a commission of inquiry to act in a fair and unbiased manner and within its terms of reference," Richwhite said.
"The recent disclosure of secret evidence has compounded our concerns that this has not been the approach taken by the Commission," he said.
Richwhite said he was not bringing the application for review in order to further delay the Commission's proceedings or to prevent Davison from reporting.
"Nothing would give me greater pleasure than to see this Commission complete its work and report in a fair and unbiased manner within its terms of reference," Richwhite said.

"However, Fay Richwhite, its directors and officers, have been so severely disadvantaged by the way in which Sir Ronald has conducted this inquiry that there was no alternative but to make application to the High Court," he said.
Richwhite said Davison's confidentiality order on the transcripts meant that Fay Richwhite could not give further details on the statement of claim.
Consequently, it was inappropriate to make any further comment, he said.
Richwhite, citing legal concerns, declined to answer questions from journalists at the hastily called news conference held at the company's Queen Street office.
